problem: Navigating to the nearest destination type in an unseen city from local street-view images. Prior work (Khosla et al.) used hand-crafted HOG features plus SVR, and deep RL does not scale to city-sized environments with very sparse rewards (about 30 goals in ~100k locations).
motivation: Cities share structure across environments (e.g. gas stations near freeway exits, restaurants in business districts). An agent that learns this structure could explore unknown man-made environments efficiently. A* on the city graph is an oracle that can label every image automatically, so supervised learning is preferable to sparse-reward RL.
key_idea: Train VGG-16 CNNs on Google Street View graphs of cities, with A*-generated labels (distance, optimal action, or pairwise favorable direction), to choose the direction at each intersection toward the nearest destination type in held-out cities.
insight: Letting the network compare views in all directions (Siamese DeepNav-pair) gives the best mean success at ds=470m (59.95, vs 56.21 for distance and 42.55 for direction). Forward-only DeepNav-direction yields short paths but low success, so it works only at short range. Geographic weighting of the loss was needed for SGD to converge on direction and pair. Deep features beat HOG+SVR (56.21 vs 54.63 mean success at 470m), but gains over random walk remain modest at long range.
method: City graph dataset: nodes are (25m-bin location, N/S/E/W heading) with a 640x480, 90° FoV Street View crop; directed edges along roads plus in-place turning edges; 10 cities, ~1M images; destinations (BofA, church, gas station, high school, McDonald's) found via Google Places and snapped to roads with the Roads API.

DeepNav-distance: VGG-16 with fc8 replaced by 5 outputs regressing sqrt of the straight-line distance to the nearest destination of each class within the image's 90° arc (Euclidean loss); test-time greedy step toward the direction with the lowest estimated distance.
DeepNav-direction: fc8 with 20 outputs (4 actions x 5 classes) trained with softmax loss on A*-optimal action labels; test time uses only the forward-facing image.

DeepNav-pair: Siamese VGG with tied weights over pairs of images at the same location; A* marks at most one image per pair as favorable and a softmax loss is applied across the pair; at test time all directions are scored and the highest is chosen.

A* label generation: for each node, A* finds the shortest path to the nearest destination and labels the nodes along the path with the optimal action or pair preference, repeated per destination class.
Geographically weighted loss: sample weight λ^l (λ=0.9), where l is the shortest-path length to a destination, used for direction and pair models.
Training: Caffe SGD, initialized from VGG-16, 8 epochs, ~72h per model on a TITAN X; the agent may not repeat the same action at a node.

setting.backbone: VGG-16 (ImageNet-pretrained, fine-tuned; Siamese variant for pair)
setting.training_data: ~1M Google Street View images (6 training cities: Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Houston, Los Angeles, Philadelphia) with automatically generated A* labels; ImageNet-pretrained init
setting.observation: monocular RGB street-view crops (90° FoV) in each navigable direction at the current location
setting.action_space: discrete graph moves at intersections: forward / backward / left / right (composed of step and in-place turn)
setting.simulator: Custom Google Street View city graphs (real imagery)
setting.privileged: none at test time (A* baseline uses the full graph and goal but is a reference only)

numbers.eval_set_note: 4 held-out cities (Dallas, New York, Phoenix, San Francisco), ~250 start locations per city, ds=470m, 5 destination classes
numbers.extra: success radius 75m, max 1000 steps; mean over cities and destinations
numbers.evidence: Table 2 (expected steps, ds=470m), Table 3 mean success 59.95, Table 4 mean 257.25

numbers_note: Custom benchmark, not one of the canonical ones. Best variant differs by ds: DeepNav-distance has slightly better expected steps at 690m (684.22) and 970m (773.02) than pair; the entries above list only pair at these ranges. The paper does not report SPL.
results: DeepNav-pair achieves the best mean success (59.95%) and expected steps (553.39) at ds=470m, versus HOG+SVR at 54.63% and 588.66 and random walk at 39.77% and 733.99. The gap narrows at longer distances (at 690m and 970m DeepNav-distance is marginally better in expected steps), and all methods remain far from A* (18.73 to 39.57 steps).
limitations: Gains over random walk and HOG+SVR are modest, and agents still need hundreds of steps versus tens for A*; performance degrades with start distance.
Only 5 destination classes and 10 US cities are used, with a greedy myopic policy without memory (only a no-repeat-action rule to avoid loops).
Each model takes ~72 hours to train, and the direction/pair models need geographic weighting to converge.
builds_on: Khosla et al. Looking Beyond the Visible Scene (HOG+SVR)
